findings.note: Item 'Who can sell the house if the owner cannot or will not?' states as flat law: "Only someone with legal authority to sign." and "Living in the house does not give that authority." No ledger claim supports a statement about who has authority to sell or what living in a house confers. The list (owner, trustee, executor or administrator, several heirs who agree) is also uncited. Rewrite as a careful, non-conclusive statement, for example that the person living in the house may not be the person with authority, and that who can sign depends on how title is held and must be confirmed with an attorney or title company.

Hedge ruling: reword. "Not always." implies there are cases where a seller must clean out, and no ledger claim or stored passage supports either a duty or the absence of one. Open the answer with wording the evidence supports, such as that the choice depends on time, money, authority and route, without implying a legal cleanout rule either way.
